title: 90+ Opus 5.5 AI Agents Find 2 Magnetic Semiconductors in 3 Days
summary:
The chemical compounds YBaMnFeO₅ and KV[Cr(CN)₆] have been identified as candidates for electronics that manipulate electron spin at temperatures above freezing. A network of 90+ Opus 5.5 AI agents isolated the materials in 3 days by running hundreds of quantum-mechanical simulations, specifically density functional theory, on cloud computers. The simulations predict a 2.35 eV band gap for YBaMnFeO₅ and a 2.1 eV gap for KV[Cr(CN)₆), with both materials maintaining magnetism above room temperature.

Researchers have sought materials that sort electrons by spin while their magnetism cancels for decades. While YBaMnFeO₅ is a new design, researchers note that the required Mn/Fe checkerboard structure may scramble during synthesis. KV[Cr(CN)₆] was first synthesized in 1999 and is measured as magnetic up to 376 K, meaning its potential as a spin-sorting material remained unnoticed for 27 years.

selectedTweets.text:
As far as we know, YBaMnFeO₅ is a new design that was never made or proposed as this kind of magnet. Simulations predict a 2.35 eV band gap and magnetism above room temperature, but the Mn/Fe checkerboard it needs may scramble during synthesis.

KV[Cr(CN)₆] stays magnetic up to 376 K (measured, 1999). We predict a 2.1 eV gap with both band edges in one spin channel, sorted over 2.6 and 1.6 eV windows.

To verify, the agents ran hundreds of quantum-mechanical simulations (density functional theory, the standard way to compute how electrons behave in a crystal) on cloud computers.
